full_judgment:
2. Facts, in short, are that the respondent No.1 by the letter dated June 8, 1997 of the Ministry of Law, Justice and 'Parliamentary Affairs (Solicitor Wing), Government of Bangladesh was appointed along with another Advocate as the Special Public Prosecutors to conduct hearing of the Sessions Case No. 120 of 1993. The respondent No. 1 while conducting hearing of the aforesaid-Session case, the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Solicitor Wing), by its letter dated 13-9-1998 cancelled appointment of the respondent No.1  mentioning “..... বিরুদ্ধে অভিযোগ উত্থাপিত হওয়ায় সরকার তাহার নিয়োগ বাতিল পূর্বক উপরোক্ত মামলা পরিচালনার জন্য সুপ্রিমকোর্ট বারের এ্যাডভোকেট জনাব খোন্দকার আব্দুল মান্নানকে বিশেষ পিপি হিসাবে নিয়োগ প্রদান করিলেন।” 

 The Rule was contested by filing affidavit-in-opposition by the writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 i.e. Secretary and the Assistant Secretary of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs as well as by the added respondents who are facing trial in the aforementioned Sessions Case by reiterating the statements made by respondent Nos.1 and 2 in their affidavit-in-opposition. 

 4. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 in their affidavit-in-opposition have stated that the allegation of malafide in cancelling the appointment of the writ- petitioner is not correct and that the allegation that cancellation of the appointment of writ-petitioner was made for collateral purpose is also not correct. It was also stated by the respondent Nos.1 and 2 in their affidavit-in-opposition that some of the witnesses of the Session Case made representation to the Government that the writ-petitioner on several occasions instructed them to depose as tutored by him and that in spite of the direction from the superior Court for disposal of the Session Case expeditiously, the writ-petitioner repeatedly took adjournments and he only examined 7 witnesses out of 36 witnesses in one year and three months i.e. from the date of his appointment, and thus the respondents being dissatisfied with his performance cancelled the appointment of the writ-petitioner, that in cancelling the appointment of the writ- petitioner no imputation in any respect was levelled against him and that letter of termination does not carry any stigma on the professional reputation of the writ-petitioner, that as per provision of section 492 of the Code of Criminal Procedure read with the provision in Legal Remembrancer's Manual, the Government is quite competent to terminate the appointment of the Special Public Procedure at any time without assigning any reason and particularly, when Government is not satisfied with the performance of the Special Public Prosecutor, that as per provision of section 492 of the Code of Criminal Procedure read with the provision in Legal Remembrancer's Manual it is not necessary to serve show cause notice before terminating appointment of the Special Public Prosecutor or Public Prosecutor, that Senior Public Prosecutor having had resigned Government felt necessity of appointing a comparatively senior and experienced lawyer to conduct hearing of the Sessions Case and accordingly, appointed Mr Kh Abdul Mannan as the Special Public Prosecutor, that writ-petitioner's appointment was term inated in the interest of fair prosecution of the Session Case and to ensure justice and that also for expeditious disposal of the Session Case, that the writ-petitioner was appointed as Special Public Prosecutor to conduct hearing of the Session Case No.120 of 1993 alone and, as such, he did not acquire any legal right and further terms and conditions of the service as of Special Public Prosecutor is not governed or regulated by any law and statutory rule and, as such, the writ petition so filed is not maintainable. 

 9. As to maintainability of the writ petition, the High Court Division upon referring to the provision of Article 31 of the Constitution held "This article specifically provides for the protection against any action detrimental to his reputation. The impugned Memo may be detrimental to the reputation of the petitioner. This Court under Article 102 of the Constitution is competent and within its jurisdiction to protect this right and pass any order for its protection under Article 102 of the Constitution. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that this application filed by the petitioner under Article 102 of the Constitution is maintainable being a person aggrieved by the impugned Memo which is claimed to be detrimental to his career and reputation." 

 11. The learned Advocate (appearing with the leave of the Court) for the respondent No.1 (writ-petitioner) has submitted that provision of Article 31 of the Constitution guarantees protection to the respondent No.1 against any action detrimental to his reputation and since the letter of termination carries a stigma against the respondent No.1 and as the same is detrimental to the reputation. and career of the respondent No.1 and that as damage to the reputation and career of the respondent No.1 has been caused by public functionary, the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division has rightly been invoked seeking declaration that the Memo carrying stigma against the respondent No.1 is illegal and without jurisdiction. The learned Advocate also submitted that although appointment of the respondent No.1 as Special Public Prosecutor was terminated with stigma or, in other words, making imputation on the integrity of the respondent No.1 in conducting hearing of the Session Case but no opportunity was given to him to put forward his version of the matter or, in other words, he was condemned unheard and thereby as there has been serious violation of the principle of natural justice, the order of termination has rightly been found by the High Court Division illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 12. The learned Counsel, Mr Abdul Malek, representing respondent Nos. 2-16 and 18-32, has submitted that as per provision of section 492 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the Government is at liberty to appoint any particular lawyer to act as Special Public Prosecutor and, as such, Government is quite competent to cancel the appointment of the Special Public Prosecutor or Public Prosecutor at any point of time and that the Government having had exercised its power of cancelling the appointment of the respondent No.1 (writ-petitioner) to act as the Special Public Prosecutor in conducting hearing of the Session Case No.120 of 1993 the writ petition challenging such removal was not maintainable and, as such, the High Court Division was in error in declaring the order cancelling appointment of the writ-petitioner as Public Prosecutor illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 14. The respondent No.1 was appointed to conduct hearing of Session Case No. 120 of 1993 in the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka and that later on by the letter impugned in the writ petition his appointment as Special Public Prosecutor was cancelled mentioning “বিরুদ্ধে আভিযোগ উখাপিত হওয়ায় সরকার তাহার নিয়োগ বাতিল পূর্বক...............।” 

 The respondent No.1 has moved as against the order terminating his appointment as Special Public Prosecutor primarily contending that his appointment has been cancelled with a stigma and that as his appointment has been cancelled with a stigma the same is detrimental to his reputation and to his career as an Advocate. It may be mentioned the High Court Division in its judgment has observed that in terminating the appointment of the respondent No.1 no specific allegation was made against him, but in spite of that proceeded with the view that although no specific allegation has been made against the respondent No.1 in the letter of termination but the letter of termination carries stigma on the respondent No. 1 and, as such, removal of the respondent No.1 without hearing him was violation of the principle of natural justice. We have already quoted the words upon mentioning which the appointment of the respondent No.1 as Special Public Prosecutor was terminated. On a reading of those words we are of the view the said words can neither be considered to convey stigma directly or indirectly in respect of the respondent No.1, nor imputation on the respondent No.1's professional career or detrimental to the reputation and career of the respondent No.1 since the words in the letter of termination are unspecified and vague. The High Court Division itself also has observed that no specific allegation was made in respect of the respondent No. 1 in the letter by which his appointment as Special Public Prosecutor was terminated. Since there had been no imputation in any respect on the professional conduct of the respondent No. 1 while terminating his appointment as Special Public Prosecutor we are of the view the appellants were not required to serve show cause notice on the respondent No.1 before issuing the letter of termination as impugned in the writ petition and, in that view of the matter, the appellants in not issuing any show cause notice before issuing the letter of termination have not violated the principle of natural justice, nor can it be said the respondent No.1 was condemned unheard. As we have already held that as no specific or definite imputation was made by the appellants on the respondent No.1's professional career in terminating his appointment as Special Public Prosecutor and, consequent thereupon, as the letter so impugned in the writ petition did not contain anything detrimental to the reputation and career of the respondent No.1 there was no violation of the provision of Article 31 of the Constitution and, as such; the writ petition so filed was not maintainable. It may be mentioned the respondent No.1 was appointed to act as Special Public Prosecutor for conducting the hearing of the Session Case No.120 of 1993 and the appointment so made under section 492 of the Code of Criminal Procedure carried with it power of termination on the circumstances as stated hereinbefore from the office of Public Prosecutor or Special Public Prosecutor. The relationship between the Special Public Prosecutor so appointed under section 492 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Government was that of a client and a lawyer and that being the accepted position, the person as in the instant case, whose skill or specialised knowledge the Government was utilising can hardly take exception to the letter communicating decision discontinuing utilisation of his service in future. The step so taken by the litigant, herein Government, the lawyer engaged earlier by the litigant can hardly take exception thereto. In the instant case as same had happened, the respondent No.1 under misconception of fact and his position in law moved the High Court Division in writ jurisdiction questioning legality of the communication made to him informing discontinuation of utilisation of service he was rendering.
